summary: Rollback/pin race during canary rollout causes traffic to unexpectedly fallback to legacy model
description: Issue summary: Customer StorifyAI reported that during a canary rollout of model storify/generative-story-2.1:v1.5 the service suddenly started routing a subset of traffic to an older legacy model (redwood/gpt-base-1.0) despite a customer pin to v1.4. Impact: ~18% of requests for the pinned route returned older-model outputs with higher latency and lower quality; customer reports production users seeing degraded results and increased error rate in downstream metrics. Environment: prod/us-east (dedicated cluster for StorifyAI).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer has route 'storify-story-gen' pinned to storify/generative-story-2.1:v1.4
2) Customer triggers canary rollout to v1.5 (10% initial traffic) via Redwood Console
3) Shortly after canary started, some requests intended for pinned route began returning outputs from redwood/gpt-base-1.0
4) Observed behavior is intermittent (~1 in 5 requests for certain prefixes) and correlated with autoscaler activity on the dedicated pool
logs_and_metrics: Ingress logs: 2026-03-10T15:23:11Z route=storify-story-gen decision=fallback target=redwood/gpt-base-1.0 reason=route_unavailable
Serving runtime logs: 2026-03-10T15:23:12Z allocation: node-17 drained during scale-down (trace_id=abc123)
Latency spike: median p95 increased from 210ms -> 680ms for affected requests between 15:23-15:40 UTC
Error trend: 502 responses rose from 0.2% -> 3.4% in the same window
comments: Leah Kim (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer opened ticket after noticing quality regression on production. Provided request examples and timestamps. Asked for immediate mitigation and explanation.
Marco Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged, escalated to routing team. Asked customer to hold traffic for canary and provided temporary config to force route to pinned version via console override.

Priya Nair (Routing Eng) 2026-03-11: Initial hypothesis — routing decision tree prioritized 'available model variants' ahead of 'customer pin' during a concurrent state transition (scale-down / rollout). Reproduced locally with scale-down simulation. Filing PR to change routing precedence.

Sophie Chen (Customer Success) 2026-03-11: Applied temporary workaround for StorifyAI: manually re-bound pin to the exact instance hash and disabled auto-burst for the route. Customer confirmed immediate reduction in legacy model hits.

Marco Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-12: Patch merged to staging (PR#981). Will schedule canary deploy of routing change to prod on 2026-03-13 after 24h soak in staging. Leaving ticket open until prod rollout and customer validation.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Race between pin update and orchestrator scale-down — when a node drained, the routing table temporarily marked the pinned variant as 'unavailable' and fallback rules sent traffic to any compatible model; because fallback selection did not check for explicit customer pins, it selected legacy model.
Hypothesis 2: Canary affinity layer not honoring pinned route metadata when route state transitions overlap (canary rollout + manual pin update close in time).

Finding: Reproduction in staging when inducing pod termination during canary rollout. Logs show routing decision path: availability check -> fallback pick -> (no pin check) -> select compatible model. Confirmed missing pin precedence in routing code path.

Related: This behavior is similar but not identical to SUP-4721. That ticket involved misroute during canary, but here the core issue is routing precedence logic missing 'pin' guard during concurrent state transitions.
resolution: Workaround provided: customer re-bound pin to exact model instance hash and we disabled automatic burst routing for their route; this prevented further legacy-model hits. Temporary console override instructions sent. Permanent fix: Routing precedence corrected to evaluate explicit customer pins before evaluating fallback candidates. Patch implemented in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/981, merged to staging 2026-03-12. Prod rollout scheduled 2026-03-13 with targeted canary. Post-deploy validation plan: monitor legacy-model hit rate, p95 latency, and 5xx for 24h. Follow-up: runbook update to include manual override steps and add automated alert when pinned variant becomes unavailable during a rollout.
